whereas the **full model** is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{logit}(\mu_i)
&=
\beta_0
+
\beta_1x_{i,1}
+
\beta_2x_{i,2}
+
\beta_3x_{i,3},\\
\log(\phi_i)
&=
\gamma_0
+
\gamma_1x_{i,1}
+
\gamma_2x_{i,2}
+
\gamma_3x_{i,3}.
\end{aligned}
$${#eq-beta-joint-test-full}

Thus, the two models have the **same precision-submodel structure** and differ only through the three non-reference `Study Time` coefficients in the mean submodel. The reduced model is obtained from the full model by imposing

$$
\beta_1=\beta_2=\beta_3=0.
$$

Importantly, preserving the same precision structure does not mean fixing the precision coefficients at identical numerical estimates across the two fits. The $\gamma$ coefficients are nuisance parameters for this test and are **estimated by maximum likelihood under each competing model**.

Then, the hypotheses are

$$
\begin{gathered}
H_0\text{: }\beta_1=\beta_2=\beta_3=0,\\
\text{versus}\\
H_1\text{: }\text{at least one of }\beta_1,\beta_2,\beta_3\neq0.
\end{gathered}
$$

Under $H_0$, the four study-time categories share the same conditional mean, although their fitted precisions are still allowed to differ. The full model adds three mean coefficients, so the likelihood-ratio statistic is compared with an asymptotic $\chi^2_3$ reference distribution. Now, let us proceed to the test.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## **`R`**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| label: tbl-beta-testing-lrt-r
#| tbl-cap: "Testing-set likelihood-ratio test for the study time terms in the conditional-mean submodel."
#| message: false
#| warning: false

beta_testing_reduced_model <- betareg(
  grade_beta ~ 1 | `Study Time`, data = testing_data,
  link = "logit", link.phi = "log", type = "ML", dist = "beta",
  control = betareg.control(method = "BFGS")
)

beta_testing_lr_statistic <- 2 * (
  as.numeric(logLik(beta_testing_refit)) -
    as.numeric(logLik(beta_testing_reduced_model))
)
stopifnot(beta_testing_lr_statistic > -1e-6)
beta_testing_lr_statistic <- max(0, beta_testing_lr_statistic)
beta_testing_lr_df <- 3L
beta_testing_lr_p_value <- pchisq(
  beta_testing_lr_statistic, df = beta_testing_lr_df, lower.tail = FALSE)

beta_format_p_value <- function(value) {
  ifelse(value < 0.001, "<0.001",
    formatC(value, format = "f", digits = 3))
}

beta_testing_lrt <- tibble(
  `LR statistic` = beta_testing_lr_statistic,
  df = beta_testing_lr_df,
  `p-value` = beta_format_p_value(beta_testing_lr_p_value))

beta_testing_lrt |>
  kable(digits = 3, align = c("c", "c", "c"))
```

## **`Python`**

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

beta_testing_reduced_model = BetaModel.from_formula(
    'grade_beta ~ 1',
    data=testing_data,
    exog_precision_formula=
        'C(Q("Study Time"), Treatment(reference="<1 hour"))',
    link=sm.families.links.Logit(), link_precision=sm.families.links.Log(),
).fit(method="bfgs", maxiter=1000, disp=False)

beta_testing_lr_statistic = 2 * (
    beta_testing_refit.llf - beta_testing_reduced_model.llf)
assert beta_testing_lr_statistic > -1e-6
beta_testing_lr_statistic = max(0.0, beta_testing_lr_statistic)
beta_testing_lr_df = 3
beta_testing_lr_p_value = stats.chi2.sf(
    beta_testing_lr_statistic, beta_testing_lr_df)

def beta_format_p_value(value):
    return "<0.001" if value < 0.001 else f"{value:.3f}"

beta_testing_lrt = pd.DataFrame({
    "LR statistic": [beta_testing_lr_statistic],
    "df": [beta_testing_lr_df],
    "p-value": [beta_format_p_value(beta_testing_lr_p_value)],
})
beta_testing_lrt_html = scrollable_table_html(
    beta_testing_lrt, float_format=lambda value: f"{value:.3f}")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-beta-testing-lrt-py
#| tbl-cap: "Testing-set likelihood-ratio test for the study time terms in the conditional-mean submodel."
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: asis

cat("\n", py$beta_testing_lrt_html, "\n", sep = "")
```

:::

For the canonical testing sample, the **likelihood-ratio statistic** is `r formatC(beta_testing_lr_statistic, format = "f", digits = 3)` with `r beta_testing_lr_df` degrees of freedom, giving a $p$-value `r ifelse(beta_testing_lr_p_value < 0.001, "< 0.001", paste0("= ", formatC(beta_testing_lr_p_value, format = "f", digits = 3)))`. At $\alpha=0.05$, this `r ifelse(beta_testing_lr_p_value < 0.05, "provides evidence against the null hypothesis that the four study-time categories share the same conditional mean", "does not provide sufficient evidence against the null hypothesis that the four study-time categories share the same conditional mean")`. This conclusion concerns the **mean submodel only**. Because `Study Time` remains in the precision submodel under both hypotheses, the test does not ask whether the complete conditional Beta distributions are identical across categories. It asks whether allowing the conditional mean itself to vary by `Study Time` improves the testing-data likelihood, conditional on the already frozen precision structure.

Therefore, the joint test addresses the **overall contribution of `Study Time` to the conditional mean**, but it does not identify which category contrasts are responsible for the evidence or how large those differences are on the original grade scale. We will address those questions next through coefficient-level inference and, more importantly for substantive interpretation, testing-set fitted conditional mean grades and percentage-point contrasts. As throughout the chapter, these differences are interpreted as **model-based associations**, not causal effects of changing a student's study time.

#### Coefficient-level Inference {#sec-beta-coefficient-inference}

The previous likelihood-ratio test answers the **joint question** of whether the three non-reference `Study Time` coefficients in the mean submodel are all zero. We now turn to the corresponding **coefficient-level** questions. Note that the inferential @tbl-beta-testing-coefficient-inference-r should be read through the hypothesis-test and confidence-interval machinery that produces it, rather than as a collection of isolated software outputs. The required model-based covariance matrix comes from the maximum-likelihood framework developed in @sec-beta-estimation.

![Image by [*Manfred Steger*](https://pixabay.com/users/manfredsteger-1848497/?utm_source=link-attribution&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=image&utm_content=3699345) via [*Pixabay*](https://pixabay.com/vectors/pixel-cells-pixel-to-learn-safari-3699332/).](img/safari.png){width="530"}

For each non-reference study-time coefficient $\beta_j$, where $j\in\{1,2,3\}$, we consider the two-sided hypotheses

$$
H_{0,j}\text{: }\beta_j=0
\qquad\text{versus}\qquad
H_{1,j}\text{: }\beta_j\neq 0.
$$

Recall that $\beta_j$ is a **logit-mean contrast** with the `<1 hour` reference category. Therefore, $H_{0,j}$ states that category $j$ has the same conditional mean grade proportion as the reference category on the model scale; whereas $H_{1,j}$ states that the two conditional means differ.

Now, let

$$
\widehat{\operatorname{SE}}
\left(
\widehat{\beta}_j
\right)
$$

denote the model-based SE obtained from the relevant diagonal element of the estimated joint covariance matrix of the mean and precision-submodel coefficient estimators, as discussed in @sec-beta-estimation. The Wald statistic is

$$
Z_j
=
\frac{
\widehat{\beta}_j-0
}{
\widehat{\operatorname{SE}}
\left(
\widehat{\beta}_j
\right)
}.
$$

Under $H_{0,j}$, the usual maximum-likelihood regularity conditions, and an adequately specified Beta regression model,

$$
Z_j
\;\dot{\sim}\;
\mathcal{N}(0,1).
$$

Because the alternative is two-sided, the corresponding large-sample $p$-value is

$$
p_j
=
2
\Pr
\left(
Z\geq
\left|
z_{j,\mathrm{obs}}
\right|
\right),
\qquad
Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1).
$$

A coefficient-wise 95% Wald CI is

$$
\widehat{\beta}_j
\pm
z_{0.975}
\widehat{\operatorname{SE}}
\left(
\widehat{\beta}_j
\right),
$$

where $z_{0.975}\approx1.96$. If this interval excludes $0$, the corresponding two-sided Wald test rejects $H_{0,j}$ at the 5% level. Exponentiating the endpoints gives a 95% CI for the multiplicative contrast in

$$
\frac{\mu}{1-\mu},
$$

so that

$$
\left[
\exp(L_j),
\exp(U_j)
\right]
$$

is the exponentiated interval when $[L_j,U_j]$ is the coefficient-scale CI.

::: {.Heads-up}
:::: {.Heads-up-header}
Heads-up on what these Wald results mean!
::::
:::: {.Heads-up-container}
These are **large-sample, model-based** inferential results. The precision coefficients are estimated jointly with the mean coefficients and therefore contribute to the fitted likelihood and covariance structure; **they are not treated as known constants**. @tbl-beta-testing-coefficient-inference-r below reports the mean-submodel coefficients because those coefficients answer the chapter's inferential question.

![Image by [*Manfred Steger*](https://pixabay.com/users/manfredsteger-1848497/) via [*Pixabay*](https://pixabay.com/vectors/pixel-cells-emotion-pressure-6230208/).](img/surprise.png){width="475"}

Also, the three coefficient-wise $p$-values and 95% CIs are **individual Wald summaries**, not simultaneous familywise intervals. The pre-specified joint likelihood-ratio test, in the previous subsection, remains the primary overall test of whether `Study Time` contributes to the conditional mean.
::::
:::

We now compute the coefficient-level quantities from the same fixed testing-set refit.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## **`R`**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| label: tbl-beta-testing-coefficient-inference-r
#| tbl-cap: "Coefficient-level inference for the conditional-mean submodel of the frozen testing-set Beta regression."
#| message: false
#| warning: false

beta_testing_mean_parameters <- beta_testing_refit_parameters[1:4]
beta_testing_mean_standard_errors <- beta_testing_refit_standard_errors[1:4]
beta_testing_mean_z <- beta_testing_mean_parameters / beta_testing_mean_standard_errors
beta_testing_mean_p <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(beta_testing_mean_z))
beta_testing_wald_critical <- qnorm(0.975)
beta_testing_mean_ci_lower <- beta_testing_mean_parameters -
  beta_testing_wald_critical * beta_testing_mean_standard_errors
beta_testing_mean_ci_upper <- beta_testing_mean_parameters +
  beta_testing_wald_critical * beta_testing_mean_standard_errors

beta_testing_coefficient_inference <- tibble(
  Term = c("Intercept (<1 hour)", "1–3 hours vs <1 hour",
    "3–5 hours vs <1 hour", "5+ hours vs <1 hour"),
  Estimate = unname(beta_testing_mean_parameters),
  `Model-based SE` = unname(beta_testing_mean_standard_errors),
  `Wald z` = unname(beta_testing_mean_z),
  `p-value` = unname(beta_testing_mean_p),
  `95% CI lower` = unname(beta_testing_mean_ci_lower),
  `95% CI upper` = unname(beta_testing_mean_ci_upper),
  `Exponentiated coefficient` = exp(unname(beta_testing_mean_parameters)))

beta_testing_coefficient_inference_display <- beta_testing_coefficient_inference |>
  mutate(`p-value` = vapply(`p-value`, beta_format_p_value, character(1)))

beta_testing_coefficient_inference_display |>
  kable(digits = 3, align = rep("c", 8))
```
